exposure: Women who developed VTE during puerperium
Women who developed VTE later in life
cohort: 95,257 women who gave birth between 1988 and 1998
finding: Maternal age, grandmultiparity, pregnancy-related hypertension, cesarean delivery, obesity, stillbirth, and peripartum hysterectomy are independent risk factors for developing venous thromboembolism (VTE), with cesarean delivery and blood transfusion being predictive of early VTE.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was an independent risk factor for VTE and was predictive of early VTE compared to late VTE.
